title: SQL avanzado y modelado relacional

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of S29.json returned 404 before creation.

learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S26-S28 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED. S29 must not treat print-only tests, hardcoded promotion states, or unverified history/provenance as trusted inputs.

roadmap_expectation.gate: Preserve source records, entities, candidate pairs, decisions and evidence without overwriting history.

live_surface.card_tagline: Almacén relacional del ER: fuentes, entidades, pares, decisiones append-only y evidencia — con constraints, consultas de cola y transacciones atómicas en SQLite de laboratorio

runtime_counterexamples.observed: A second row with the same (e1,e2) and a different id is accepted because canonical DDL omits UNIQUE(entity_a,entity_b).
True is accepted and stored as REAL 1.0; string '0.5' is accepted and stored as REAL 0.5.
UPDATE decisions SET label='match' succeeds and DELETE FROM decisions succeeds; append-only is a convention, not an invariant.
The ACID demo schema accepts evidence(pair_id='missing-pair') because no FK binds evidence to a decision or candidate pair.
With p1-p3 top scores already decided and p4-p5 undecided, canonical query returns [] while filter-then-rank returns p4,p5.
Repo schema accepts same-entity pair, reversed pair, and score=9.0.
A pair with decision label='review' is excluded by NOT EXISTS(any decision), although 'review' denotes unresolved human handling elsewhere in the same section.

external_research_basis: SQLite foreign keys are per-connection and currently default OFF; applications should set the required state explicitly.
SQLite ordinary tables use type affinity rather than rigid typing; STRICT tables are available when rigid table typing is desired.
SQLite CHECK fails on numeric zero; NULL is not itself a CHECK violation, so NOT NULL and domain checks are separate contracts.
SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output is for interactive debugging and its output format may change; SCAN/SEARCH details should be interpreted rather than matched as a stable application API.
SQLite UPSERT is triggered by uniqueness constraints and can condition DO UPDATE with a WHERE clause, including freshness/version checks.
SQLite serializes writes across connections and BEGIN IMMEDIATE has specific concurrency semantics; one :memory: connection does not demonstrate those behaviors.
Python sqlite3 maps Python None to SQL NULL and currently recommends explicit autocommit-based transaction control.
Testcontainers can run tests against the same type of service used in production instead of relying only on in-memory substitutes.
Alembic models migrations as revision artifacts/graphs with upgrade/downgrade/current-state semantics; a row in schema_migrations alone is not equivalent to an executable migration system.

findings.title: PREREQUISITE_REGRESSION_DEBT_LAUNDERED
findings.evidence: S29 begins a truth-store layer without preserving the known critical S26 regression pack required by S28 continuation.
findings.attack: A relational store can make bad upstream success/approval labels look more authoritative simply by persisting them.
findings.defense: S29's nominal prerequisites are S12 and S28, not every prior implementation detail.
findings.impact: Risk-first testing learned in S27 is abandoned at the exact point where persistence would fossilize defects.

findings.title: PYTEST_GATE_STILL_ABSENT
findings.evidence: All eight canonical theory code blocks use prints/manual booleans; none is a collected pytest test despite S27-S28 carry-forward requiring executable repository/transaction/migration tests.
findings.attack: Wrong SQL can still exit 0 if a learner only observes printed output.
findings.defense: The mini-labs are explanatory snippets, not explicitly named tests.
findings.impact: The section cannot claim tested constraints/repository behavior from its canonical theory evidence.

findings.title: CANDIDATE_MEMBERSHIP_AND_RESOLVED_MEMBERSHIP_CONFLATED
findings.evidence: Reference says a source record may link to multiple candidate entities through entity_source_links while resolution remains open.
findings.attack: Candidate hypotheses and resolved source→entity membership are different domain states; putting both into an undifferentiated membership table obscures whether a link is proposed, accepted, rejected, or superseded.
findings.defense: An N-N link table is structurally flexible and can later receive status/temporal columns.
findings.impact: S30 may consume ambiguous memberships as resolved truth.

findings.title: FOREIGN_KEY_CAUSALITY_OVERCLAIM
findings.evidence: Reference says that 'with a FK, each change of opinion would erase the previous one.'
findings.attack: A foreign key does not imply overwrite; history loss comes from storing only current membership in one mutable row rather than from FK semantics.
findings.defense: The sentence is contrasting a direct FK column with a link table in simplified language.
findings.impact: Learner may attribute temporal-model defects to the wrong relational mechanism.

findings.title: ROADMAP_TRUTH_STORE_MODEL_NOT_MATERIALIZED
findings.evidence: Theory promises source_records, entity_source_links, entities, candidate_pairs, decisions and evidence, but canonical executable model never creates the complete graph.
findings.attack: The authoritative gate requires all five artifact families to remain reconstructable.
findings.defense: Each mini-lab isolates one concept to reduce cognitive load.
findings.impact: No canonical integration proves referential integrity or history across the actual store graph.

findings.title: PAIR_UNIQUENESS_PROMISED_BUT_MISSING
findings.evidence: T1-A prose requires CHECK(entity_a<entity_b) plus UNIQUE(entity_a,entity_b), but keys_constraints.py omits UNIQUE.
findings.attack: Runtime accepted a second (e1,e2) row with another id.
findings.defense: Mirror pairs are blocked by A<B and primary-key ids are unique.
findings.impact: The same canonical candidate can exist more than once and receive divergent decisions.

findings.title: SQLITE_DYNAMIC_TYPING_BREAKS_SCORE_TYPE_CONTRACT
findings.evidence: score REAL + CHECK range accepts Python True as 1.0 and text '0.5' as 0.5 under SQLite affinity.
findings.attack: S28 required explicit type/coercion policy; S29 silently treats coercion as valid.
findings.defense: SQLite affinity and numeric coercion are legitimate engine behavior and the range remains protected.
findings.impact: A truth store can normalize wrong input types into plausible scores without recording the coercion.

findings.title: APPEND_ONLY_IS_NOT_ENFORCED
findings.evidence: decisions has no trigger/authorization layer preventing UPDATE or DELETE; runtime update and delete both succeed.
findings.attack: Calling a table append-only while ordinary write paths can rewrite/delete it is a policy claim, not a database invariant.
findings.defense: Application repository code could enforce append-only even if SQLite itself does not.
findings.impact: The core audit-history guarantee can be bypassed accidentally or by future repository methods.

findings.title: PROVENANCE_REFERENCES_ARE_UNVERIFIED_STRINGS
findings.evidence: temporality demo stores evidence_ref TEXT with no evidence table/FK and no FK from decisions.pair_id to candidate_pairs.
findings.attack: Runtime allows evidence refs/pairs that do not exist.
findings.defense: The block is scoped to event history rather than full schema integration.
findings.impact: A decision can claim evidence that cannot be resolved or reproduced.

findings.title: DECLARED_RUN_SOURCE_PROVENANCE_NOT_STORED
findings.evidence: Prose names source_system, source_record_id, ingested_at, transform_version and run_id, but temporality_prov.py stores none except a free-form evidence_ref.
findings.attack: Printing 'provenance ev_02' does not prove lineage.
findings.defense: The fields are described conceptually and could live in other tables.
findings.impact: The learner cannot reconstruct which source bytes/transformation produced the decision.

findings.title: TEMPORAL_ORDER_IS_UNDERSPECIFIED
findings.evidence: Both sample decisions receive the identical timestamp and history is ordered by surrogate id.
findings.attack: Insertion order is not the same contract as event/valid time; delayed events or imports can reorder history.
findings.defense: For this lab the rows are inserted synchronously and id ordering is deterministic.
findings.impact: The phrase 'what the reviewer saw Tuesday' is stronger than the schema can establish.

findings.title: ANY_DECISION_FALSELY_MEANS_NOT_PENDING
findings.evidence: Pending queue uses NOT EXISTS(any decisions row), while the same section inserts label='review' as a decision state.
findings.attack: A pair routed to review disappears from the review queue merely because the routing decision exists.
findings.defense: The authors may intend decisions to mean completed human decisions and 'review' as a pedagogical placeholder.
findings.impact: Queue semantics can silently hide unresolved cases.

findings.title: RANK_BEFORE_ANTIJOIN_DROPS_VALID_PENDING_CASES
findings.evidence: CTE assigns ROW_NUMBER to all pairs, applies rn<=3, then removes decided rows.
findings.attack: If top three are decided, lower-scoring pending pairs are never considered; runtime returned [] although p4,p5 were pending.
findings.defense: The three-row toy fixture does not expose the failure.
findings.impact: Top-N review capacity can be underfilled and cases starved.

findings.title: ROW_NUMBER_TIES_HAVE_NO_STABLE_TIEBREAKER
findings.evidence: ROW_NUMBER windows order only by score DESC.
findings.attack: Equal-score peers have no declared business ordering; S28 required deterministic ordering contracts.
findings.defense: Toy fixture scores are unique.
findings.impact: Queue order can change across plans/data and make tests/audits unstable.

findings.title: QUERY_PLAN_FIGURE_TEACHES_WRONG_READING_RULE
findings.evidence: Figure caption says 'El plan es un árbol y se lee de abajo hacia arriba.'
findings.attack: SQLite documentation says entry order indicates nesting: first scan is outer loop, last inner; a universal bottom-up reading rule is misleading.
findings.defense: Trees are often visually inspected from leaves toward root when reasoning about data flow.
findings.impact: Learner may misread actual EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN nesting.

findings.title: PLAN_DEMO_DOES_NOT_INSPECT_SCAN_VS_SEARCH
findings.evidence: card_null_plan.py prints only len(plan), despite prose/outcome requiring reasoning about SCAN vs SEARCH/index use.
findings.attack: A one-row plan can be a SCAN or SEARCH; row count of plan does not answer the question.
findings.defense: T4-A later demonstrates index-related plan text.
findings.impact: The T2-B observable outcome is not demonstrated where taught.

findings.title: PYTHON_NONE_SQL_NULL_WORDING_IS_MISLEADING
findings.evidence: Paragraph says 'NULL en SQL no es Python None.'
findings.attack: Python sqlite3 maps None↔NULL directly; the important difference is SQL three-valued comparison semantics, not representation mapping.
findings.defense: The intended warning is semantic, not adapter-level.
findings.impact: Learner may avoid or misunderstand correct parameter binding with None.

findings.title: DECISION_EVIDENCE_RELATIONSHIP_CONTRADICTS_MODEL
findings.evidence: T1-A says evidence is child of decision (FK decisions.id); ACID demo creates evidence(pair_id) with no decision_id or FK.
findings.attack: Atomic insertion does not prove evidence belongs to the exact decision version.
findings.defense: pair_id can group both rows in the toy lab.
findings.impact: Later decisions for the same pair can become indistinguishable from evidence intended for earlier versions.

findings.title: UPSERT_KEY_DOES_NOT_MATCH_REINGEST_CONTRACT
findings.evidence: Prose says same source_system/external_id drives reingest; upsert demo conflicts only on entities.id and stores neither source_system nor external_id.
findings.attack: The example cannot prove idempotency for the natural source identity it names.
findings.defense: Stable entity id can serve as a simplified key in the isolated example.
findings.impact: Learner may conflate source-record identity with resolved-entity identity.

findings.title: STALE_REPLAY_OVERWRITES_NEWER_ENTITY_STATE
findings.evidence: DO UPDATE always copies excluded name/updated with no freshness predicate.
findings.attack: Runtime showed updated=2/'Newest' overwritten by replay updated=1/'Stale'. SQLite supports a WHERE predicate on DO UPDATE for this purpose.
findings.defense: The toy example assumes arrivals are ordered.
findings.impact: Recovery/retry can regress canonical entity state.

findings.title: ENTITY_UPSERT_CONFLICTS_WITH_ROADMAP_HISTORY_GATE
findings.evidence: Roadmap gate says source records, entities, candidate pairs, decisions and evidence remain preserved without overwriting history; T3-B overwrites entity attributes in place.
findings.attack: Only decision history is protected; entity state history is destroyed.
findings.defense: Roadmap can be read as preserving decision/evidence history while allowing mutable canonical attributes.
findings.impact: The truth store cannot reconstruct which canonical entity attributes were visible when a decision was made.

findings.title: INTEGRITYERROR_IS_MISCLASSIFIED_AS_RETRYABLE
findings.evidence: T3-B recommends retry if IntegrityError occurs from conflict.
findings.attack: IntegrityError covers UNIQUE/FK/CHECK/NOT NULL; many are deterministic data/invariant failures, and duplicate pair conflicts need idempotent resolution rather than blind retry.
findings.defense: The sentence specifically mentions pair conflict under concurrent workers.
findings.impact: Retries can loop or hide malformed data instead of resolving concurrency safely.

findings.title: RESTART_AND_IDEMPOTENCY_ARE_CLAIMED_NOT_TESTED
findings.evidence: Prose says crash jobs return to pending and reapply idempotently, but all demos use :memory: and no reopen/checkpoint path exists.
findings.attack: An in-memory DB vanishes on process restart.
findings.defense: True multi-connection contention is explicitly deferred to S38.
findings.impact: S28's unfinished restart requirement remains unverified at the persistence layer where it belongs.

findings.title: SCHEMA_MIGRATIONS_ROW_IS_NOT_EXECUTABLE_MIGRATION_HISTORY
findings.evidence: Mini-lab creates final schema/index and inserts (1,'init_pairs') manually.
findings.attack: No migration artifact, dependency/order check, idempotent runner, upgrade/downgrade, applied_at or checksum exists.
findings.defense: The section only introduces migration versioning, not Alembic tooling.
findings.impact: A learner can mark a migration applied without proving the schema transition occurred.

findings.title: NO_DROP_WITHOUT_BACKUP_IS_ONLY_A_SLOGAN
findings.evidence: T4-A states no_drop_without_backup but canonical code neither creates/verifies a backup nor blocks DROP.
findings.attack: The safety gate has no executable enforcement or test.
findings.defense: It is framed as policy for lab/production rather than SQLite feature.
findings.impact: Destructive migration safety is asserted without evidence.

findings.title: EXPLAIN_OUTPUT_STRING_MATCH_IS_BRITTLE
findings.evidence: indexes_migrate.py declares uses_index if plan contains idx name, USING INDEX, or generic INDEX.
findings.attack: SQLite explicitly warns EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output format can change and applications should not depend on it.
findings.defense: The prose itself notes plan text may vary and this is a teaching assertion, not production parser.
findings.impact: Learner sees a brittle text heuristic presented as a migration/index gate.

findings.title: REPOSITORY_SCHEMA_DROPS_CORE_CONSTRAINTS
findings.evidence: repo_pool_tests.py pairs table has only id PK; no FK, score CHECK, A<B or pair UNIQUE.
findings.attack: Runtime accepts same-entity, reversed and score=9 pairs.
findings.defense: The block's focus is repository shape and pending anti-join.
findings.impact: The abstraction layer silently weakens the truth-store invariants taught earlier.

findings.title: REPOSITORY_IS_NOT_TESTED
findings.evidence: T4-B says 'Prueba el repository' and callout says assert, but canonical code only prints pending/pattern/test_db.
findings.attack: There is no pytest constraint or pending test to block regression.
findings.defense: The You Do may ask the learner to add tests later.
findings.impact: The final theory block ends without satisfying its own testability outcome.

findings.title: REPOSITORY_API_IS_OVERCLAIMED
findings.evidence: Prose names get_entity, insert_decision, pending; PairRepo implements only add_pair and pending.
findings.attack: The example does not demonstrate decision transaction/history methods or entity retrieval boundaries.
findings.defense: Not every method needs to appear in one minimal repository example.
findings.impact: Learner cannot see where transaction/provenance invariants belong in the repository abstraction.

findings.title: IN_MEMORY_REPOSITORY_CANNOT_PROVE_PERSISTENCE_OR_REOPEN
findings.evidence: All repository/storage demos use sqlite :memory: on a single connection.
findings.attack: Restart, migration state, durability and connection initialization (including foreign_keys) disappear when connection closes.
findings.defense: SQLite :memory: is explicitly presented as local test substitute, not production proof.
findings.impact: Critical persistence semantics are never exercised despite being carry-forward requirements.

findings.title: DECISION_LABEL_DOMAIN_IS_UNCONSTRAINED
findings.evidence: decisions.label is TEXT NOT NULL with no CHECK/reference table for allowed states.
findings.attack: Typos such as 'mach' or ambiguous 'review' enter the truth store and directly affect queue semantics.
findings.defense: Allowed labels may be enforced in application code later.
findings.impact: State-machine correctness is not protected at the persistence boundary.

findings.title: SOURCE_LINK_DELETE_DESTROYS_HISTORY
findings.evidence: Reference says undoing a source/entity link should remove a row from entity_source_links.
findings.attack: DELETE erases exactly the membership history the roadmap requires preserving unless the link itself is versioned/evented.
findings.defense: The paragraph may mean remove current membership rather than delete audit history.
findings.impact: Entity provenance can no longer reconstruct previous linkage decisions.

findings.title: THIRD_NORMAL_FORM_IS_OVERCLAIMED
findings.evidence: T1-A equates a few anti-duplication choices with 'Normaliza a 3NF'.
findings.attack: 3NF is a dependency-based property of the complete relation design; the section neither states functional dependencies nor proves the whole model satisfies it.
findings.defense: The phrase is used as a practical design heuristic rather than a normalization proof.
findings.impact: Learner may think 'do not copy canonical_name' is a sufficient definition of 3NF.

findings.title: REDACTION_WIDOW_TERMS_AND_LANGUAGE_MIX
findings.evidence: High density of append-only, provenance, fan-out, blocking, CTE, window, anti-join, pending, upsert, pooling, acquire and repository appears with uneven Spanish anchoring.
findings.attack: The learner is at Level 3 but the section still introduces multiple new systems terms per paragraph without a stable Spanish-first glossary.
findings.defense: Many are unavoidable API/industry terms and several are glossed locally.
findings.impact: Cognitive load is spent decoding vocabulary instead of relational invariants.

rejected_false_positives: Rejected: SQLite is not a real database. It is a real relational SQL engine; the issue is claim scope, not legitimacy.
Rejected: NOT EXISTS is always faster than LEFT JOIN. The section correctly frames it primarily as safer/clearer around NULL, not as universal performance law.
Rejected: using :memory: is inherently wrong. It is useful for fast local relational tests when the claim is bounded.
Rejected: UPSERT is inherently incompatible with auditability. It is valid for mutable current-state projections if history is separately retained and stale updates are guarded.

Rejected: FOREIGN KEY behavior claim is false. SQLite currently requires explicit per-connection enablement in typical builds; the finding is about relying on the default or not materializing full FKs, not the basic PRAGMA claim.
Rejected: NULL comparisons are described incorrectly in general. The SQL three-valued-logic warning is substantially correct; only the Python None phrasing is misleading.
Rejected: the atomic rollback demo is invalid. It correctly demonstrates one-connection atomic rollback; it simply cannot prove broader isolation/durability/concurrency claims.

highest_risk_findings: S29-F06 duplicate canonical candidate pair accepted despite prose promising UNIQUE
S29-F08 decisions are mutable/deletable despite append-only truth-store claim
S29-F09/F10/F18 evidence/provenance references are not enforced or linked to exact decision versions
S29-F12/F13 review queue semantics hide review states and rank before filtering pending cases
S29-F20 stale replay overwrites newer entity state
S29-F21 entity upsert contradicts roadmap requirement to preserve entity history
S29-F22 IntegrityError is treated as retryable conflict without classifying permanent invariant failures
S29-F27 repository abstraction drops the constraints taught earlier
S29-F30 persistence/reopen behavior is never tested
S29-F32 deleting source/entity links would erase membership history
